transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Owen Chen (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (Aurora - Head of ML), Priya Singh (Aurora - Platform Eng), Marco Diaz (Aurora - CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick agenda - we'll show the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and then dig into the cost breakdown and routing policies. Owen and I will tag team.
[00:18] Jared: Sounds good. We're particularly interested in predictable latency for our public summarization endpoint, and how pricing shapes up at scale, so we'll ask questions as we go.
[00:27] Owen: Cool. Priya, Marco, if you have infra questions please jump in. I'll start by sharing the Console - give me a sec to navigate.
[00:36] (screen share noise)
[00:45] Owen: Alright on the left nav you can see Usage -> Per-route. This table is per-route aggregated metrics, so requests, avg latency P50/P95, token consumption, and estimated cost bucketed by model and time range.
[01:10] Priya: Are those costs actual billed amounts or run-rate estimates?
[01:15] Maya: They're estimated unit economics computed from token counts + model profile. We show both run-rate (projected) and historical billed where available. There's also a toggle for dedicated pricing which substitutes your committed rate.
[01:30] Marco: One quick question - how granular is routing? Can we split by region and fall back to a cheaper variant?
[01:38] Owen: Yes, routing policies can be configured by priority: region, latency SLO, cost threshold, or customer tier. You can set a policy to prefer low-cost quantized variants and fallback to full-precision only when latency SLAs require it. The Console shows hit rates for each route variant.
[01:55] (typing)
[02:10] Owen: Now I'll open a per-route dashboard - here's /api/v1/summarize which Aurora might map to. You can see token mix (prompt vs completion), average tokens per request, KV cache hit rate for repeated prefixes, and how batching changed latency distribution.
[02:35] Jared: That KV cache stat - is it automatic? We do a lot of near-duplicate calls so caching could save us a ton.
[02:42] Owen: Automatic prefix caching is enabled by default for routes that opt in; you can tune cache TTL and keys. The dashboard shows estimated saved tokens from cache hits and translates that to cost savings.
[02:55] Maya: For your sample traffic, we estimate roughly 18-25% token savings with a moderate cache TTL based on similar customers.
[03:05] Jared: Nice. Show us how cost per 1k tokens breaks down.
[03:12] Owen: Sure - here's the cost breakdown widget. Left side is model-level unit cost (hosted) and right side is per-route effective cost after batching, cache, and reserved capacity adjustments. For dedicated, we swap in committed rates and show utilization-based amortized GPU cost.
[03:33] Priya: Do you show amortized infra cost inside the same view or is that separate?
[03:38] Owen: It's in the same breakdown panel; we show three rows: raw model unit cost, infrastructure amortization (if Dedicated or Private), and net per-route cost. You can export CSV to our cost model spreadsheet.
[03:50] Marco: What's the typical GPU amortization assumption?
[03:54] Maya: We provide a default amortization for common instance types but you can override with your committed pricing and utilization assumptions to see real numbers.
[04:06] Jared: On security - we need SOC 2, audit logs, SSO SAML, and KMS integration. Do you expose logs per token or per request?
[04:16] Owen: We retain request-level logs and provide audit trails. For private deployments we can integrate with KMS/HSM; hosted customers get per-tenant encryption and optional bring-your-own-key. We have SOC 2 artifacts and a compliance pack which I'll share.
[04:30] (brief hold)
[04:40] Priya: For the benchmark, can you run a steady-state test with 250 RPS and the same prompt set? We need P95 under 250ms for our SLA.
[04:50] Maya: We can. We'll need your sample prompts and a rough token distribution; Jared you'll send that?
[04:56] Jared: Yep I'll share a normalized set and the histogram of request sizes.
[05:05] Owen: Back to the dashboard - here's the anomaly detection tab. We show baseline traffic, and if quality drops for a model we emit regression alerts tied to a prompt set so you can rollback or route to a different model variant.
[05:22] Marco: Can we run canary rollouts from Console?
[05:26] Owen: Yes - canary deploys and gradual rollouts with automatic rollback. You can tie metrics to canary success (latency, error rate, qualitative evals).
[05:35] (crosstalk)
[06:10] Maya: Quick objection we usually hear - "is hosted cheaper than self-hosting?" The short answer depends; Redwood Optimize suggests batching/quantization and caching which typically lowers unit cost and often makes hosted favorable unless you need strict isolation or have massive sustained throughput.
[06:35] Jared: We're leaning Dedicated because of predictable latency and compliance. Cost is the main blocker. Can you walk through an example month?
[06:44] Owen: Yep - here is a sample cost model. We input Aurora's projected tokens, split by route, apply batching and cache assumptions, and show 3 scenarios: hosted, dedicated moderate commit, and dedicated high commit. You can toggle GPU type assumptions.
[07:05] Priya: The delta between moderate and high commit looks large. How do you defend overcommit risk?
[07:12] Maya: We recommend a staged commit: start with a smaller reserved pool + autoscale burst and monitor utilization. The Console's utilization dashboards make it easy to measure effective throughput and identify idle capacity.
[07:26] Jared: If we did a pilot, what's the usual timeline?
[07:30] Owen: For a pilot with benchmarks and a week of steady-state traffic, typical timeline is 2-4 weeks: onboarding + security review (1 week) then benchmarking and tuning (1-2 weeks).
[07:45] Marco: Any concerns about data residency? We have EU customers, need region pinning.
[07:51] Owen: Region pinning is supported; you can enforce routing by region and ensure data stays in-region. Private deployment option covers stricter needs.
[08:05] (15 minute mark noise)
[08:12] Maya: Let's quickly recap the Console features we showed: per-route metrics, cost breakdown with amortization, caching savings, routing policies and canary rollouts, and regression alerts.
[08:22] Jared: Good. For next steps we'll want the pricing sheet and SOC2 docs. Also the per-route dashboard example so our infra lead can map routes.
[08:30] Maya: We'll send those. Owen will share security artifacts. We'll schedule a benchmark for week of May 11.
[08:38] Priya: One last nit - do you provide pre-built dashboards for common patterns like summarization and reranking?
[08:44] Owen: Yes, there are templates; I'll include the summarization template.
[08:48] Marco: Great, thanks everyone.
[08:52] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the benchmark.
[08:58] (call ends)
notes: Customer leaning Dedicated for latency and compliance
Primary success criteria: P95 < 250ms on summarization route, predictable per-request cost
Security: SOC2, KMS/BYOK, audit logs requested
